# Related surveys and how this one differs

**Prior work.** [*Decisions, Not Tokens: A Survey of Typed, Calibrated, and Machine-Native Decision Models from Classical Classifiers to Jev*](https://github.com/youzizzz1028/Awesome-Jev/blob/f3703012b0034eefe0d59936c44cd33ea11b2990/paper/main.tex) — Anonymous Authors (manuscript); “Awesome Jev contributors” (CITATION.cff); 2026-09-21 (in-text “Full working draft — 21 September 2026”). Status: public working draft; CITATION.cff type dataset; no arXiv entry located. Checked: 2026-09-23: head unchanged since the snapshot (GitHub API).
Manuscript commit: `c1347c84a2577ac699fc954fc1b2ef60bd7eb025 (2026-09-21 14:53:42 UTC)`. A Git timestamp shows when a commit was made, not when the work became public; neither this survey nor the prior draft is claimed as first.

What we credit to the prior draft: the umbrella framing of machine-native decision models, the separation of structural validity, semantic correctness, probabilistic reliability and decision utility, and a fair replication protocol with interface-level baselines. This survey adopts that separation.

What this survey adds, and what still needs verification, is in the matrix. The empirical claims about the prior draft refer to its pinned commit and may change in later versions.

| Dimension | Prior draft (Decisions, Not Tokens) | This survey | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Scope | Machine-native decision models broadly, from classical classifiers to Jev; Jev as a contemporary case study. | Jev and finite-option typed decision models: the commercial service, Jev-like implementations and systems that depend on them, with adjacent methods as background. | Prior draft abstract and §2; this survey §1. |
| Cutoff | 21 September 2026 (stated in the draft). | 23 September 2026 (snapshot) plus a same-day incremental rerun (logged). | Draft §2.3; data/search-runs.json. |
| Search & screening record | Lists databases and keyword families; no query log, hit counts or screening decisions in the repository at the pinned commit (only data/ecosystem.yml and data/resources.yml). | 17 logged arXiv queries (225 hits → 197 screened) plus a logged same-day increment; the rejected query kept; background records added by explicit ID are marked; GitHub discovery with page-level logs; single-reviewer screening disclosed. | Draft §2.3 and repository tree at f3703012; research/. |
| Recent empirical coverage | None of the 13 core arXiv IDs (2609.22753–2609.26758) appear in its 41-entry bibliography. | Every core and peripheral paper read in full; each claim stored as an evidence record with locator, scope, sample size and model version. | Draft references.bib at f3703012; data/claims.json. |
| Model lineage | Five-dimensional taxonomy (output contract, inference, learning objective, uncertainty, control); mentions the official adapter. | Six readout families with named open implementations, a derived-from edge (this-that ← decider) and explicit non-equivalence of compatible interfaces. | Draft §5; data/taxonomy.json; data/repositories.json. |
| Failure analysis | Conceptual: open-world inputs, local calibration, parallel consistency, compositional safety. | Empirical: option-name rebinding, abstain removal, Noul/Choice incoherence, per-construct confident errors, language shift, quantisation — each tied to a source. | Draft §9; this survey §6. |
| Openness audit | Evidence labels A–D (peer-reviewed, preprint, official, community). | Six independent fields per work (code, weights, data, predictions, recomputable, reproduced) and seven per repository. | Draft README; data/papers.json. |
| Recomputability | Figures described as conceptual illustrations; no data release for figures. | Every count, table and chart is generated from data/*.json by scripts in the repository; checks run in CI. | Draft Fig. 2 caption; scripts/. |
| Interactive resources | GitHub README index and figures. | Searchable website with filters, evidence drawers, exports and labelled illustrative explainers. | Both repositories. |
| Shared ground | Four evaluation layers (validity, semantic correctness, probabilistic reliability, decision utility) and a fair replication protocol. | This survey adopts the same separation and credits the draft for it; the difference lies in the evidence base, not the layering. | Draft Table 1 and §8.3. |

## Adjacent surveys cited as background

- [Uncertainty Quantification and Confidence Calibration in Large Language Models: A Survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.15850v2) — uncertainty quantification and calibration in LLMs. Survey of uncertainty quantification and calibration in LLMs.
- [From System 1 to System 2: A Survey of Reasoning Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.17419v6) — System 1 to System 2 reasoning LLMs. From System 1 to System 2: a reasoning-LLM survey whose terminology predates and is broader than the product.
- [Harnessing the Reasoning Economy: A Survey of Efficient Reasoning for Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.24377v3) — efficient reasoning / reasoning economy. Reasoning economy: compare inference budgets, not only parameter counts.
- [Decision-Focused Learning: Foundations, State of the Art, Benchmark and Future Opportunities](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.13565v4) — decision-focused learning. Decision-focused learning survey; its optimisation semantics differ from an API returning a choice.

## Remaining checks before claiming novelty in a submission

1. Re-run the survey/review queries (`Q07`, `Q08`, `Q14`) and a Google Scholar / Semantic Scholar title search on the submission date.
2. Re-read the prior draft at its latest commit and update the matrix.
3. Phrase contributions as specific artefacts (evidence records, openness audit, protocol) rather than as priority.
